text: According to the James–Lange theory of emotion, what is the correct order of events when you see a bear and feel afraid?
choices: The perception causes fear, which then causes bodily changes such as running
The bodily changes (running, racing heart) come first, and the felt emotion just is the perception of those bodily changes
Fear and the bodily changes occur simultaneously as independent effects of the perception
The emotion is a purely cognitive judgment, independent of any bodily state
explanation: James (with Lange) inverted the commonsense order: we do not run because we are afraid; we feel afraid because we perceive our own bodily responses such as running and a pounding heart. Option 0 states exactly the commonsense view James rejected; option 2 is closer to the later Cannon–Bard theory; option 3 is a purely cognitive theory of emotion he did not hold.
